items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: For the tour, the rhythm section was the same as the last tour, Bishop, De Haas and Starling.

ctx.x: There was in instrument company in Paris called Couesnon, and I knew the director Mr. Vincent very well. They were trying to push their horns into the jazz field and I had received a trumpet. They had given Dickie Wells and some other famous American musicians instruments also. Mr. Vincent did not agree to give Jimmy a tenor, but as a favour to me, he was willing to let Jimmy have a horn for a bargain price. I was responsible for seeing that Jimmy paid a certain amount every week which I personally would send to…

For the tour, the rhythm section was the same as the last tour, Bishop, De Haas and Starling. I also engaged a girl singer from Trinidad named Cecily Forde who had not been in France very long. We rehearsed for about a week, I finished at the Metro Jazz the 30th of September and we left for Aachen, Germany, the first of October and played our first concert the 2nd in Aachen. We played 70 towns from the 2nd of October until the 15th of December with only six days off.

We were in Kassel the 10th of November when someone in the orchestra had bought a U.S. army paper called Stars and Stripes in which there was an announcement that "Hot Lips Page" had died. I had seen him a few months ago and he was in good health at that time and we had not heard anything about him being sick. To my estimation the world had lost the greatest blues trumpeter who could sing them as well as play them. He also had given Lily and I an autographed recording of his, recorded on Columbia.
